eips.title: Resource-based intrinsic transaction gas
eips.summary: Listed as one of the EIPs whose gas repricing numbers were finalized and signed off.

moments.context: Jochem stated the final gas repricing results are in the context of EIP-2780, EIP-8037, and EIP-8038, and the numbers presented at ACD 90 are confirmed.

eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Gas repricing numbers finalized; its state gas creation cost referenced in multiple EIP discussions throughout the call.

moments.context: Listed alongside EIP-2780 and EIP-8038 as one of the three EIPs whose gas repricing results were signed off as final.
Jochem noted EIP-8037 introduces both execution gas and state gas, but the execution gas remains bounded by EIP-7825.
Kev referenced 8037's expected state growth at 150 million gas being roughly 120 gigabytes per year, motivating history expiry.
Toni explained EIP-8368 recalibrates the constant introduced in EIP-8037 because the dynamic recalibration was removed.

eips.title: State-access gas cost update
eips.summary: Listed as one of the three EIPs whose gas repricing numbers were finalized.

moments.context: Jochem listed EIP-8038 alongside EIP-2780 and EIP-8037 as part of the final gas repricing results.

eips.title: Gas Limit Schedule
eips.summary: Barnabas presented the gas limit schedule EIP allowing stepwise gas limit increases after Glamsterdam; CL clients weighed in.

moments.context: Barnabas described the EIP as introducing a new CL config parameter to hard-code a gas limit schedule, allowing stepwise increases to 200 million gas after the fork.

Nixo asked CL clients for affirmatives on the approach. Prysm, Lighthouse, Lodestar, and Teku confirmed support; Dustin from Nimbus expressed skeptical neutrality but did not oppose since it is optional.

eips.title: Bound Historical Data in Execution Clients
eips.summary: History expiry discussed as needed alongside gas limit increases; clients reported varying default retention windows.

moments.context: Kev raised EIP-4444 concerns about 2TB node operators needing history expiry at Hegota. Different clients reported different strategies: Nethermind drops to 6 months, Erigon about 5.5 months, Geth has rolling expiry, Besu only drops pre-merge.
Nixo asked to converge on a single history expiry number in the ETHRND history expiry channel and decide where to spec it.

eips.title: Hardfork Meta - Hegotá
eips.summary: Referenced as the Hegota hardfork meta EIP that proposed EIPs need to be merged into.

moments.context: Nixo stated that EIPs without a champion cannot be merged into 8081 (Hegota meta), and the PFI list should be final by the next call.

eips.title: Hard Limits for Transient Storage
eips.summary: Listed as one of five EIPs proposed by Helcamine that lacked a champion on the call.

moments.context: Nixo listed EIP-7971 (hard limits for transient storage) among Helcamine's proposals and asked if anyone would speak on its behalf; no one volunteered.

eips.title: Contract Bytecode Deduplication Discount
eips.summary: Listed as one of five EIPs proposed by Helcamine that lacked a champion on the call.

moments.context: Nixo listed EIP-8058 (contract bytecode deduplication discount) among Helcamine's proposals; no champion present to speak about it.

eips.title: Decrease base cost of TLOAD/TSTORE
eips.summary: Listed as one of five EIPs proposed by Helcamine that lacked a champion on the call.

moments.context: Nixo listed EIP-7609 (decrease base cost of TLOAD/TSTORE) among Helcamine's proposals; no champion present.

eips.title: Warm Account Write Metering
eips.summary: Listed as one of five EIPs proposed by Helcamine that lacked a champion on the call.

moments.context: Nixo listed EIP-7973 (warm account write metering) among Helcamine's proposals; no champion present.

eips.title: TCREATE Opcode
eips.summary: Listed as one of five EIPs proposed by Helcamine that lacked a champion on the call.

moments.context: Nixo added EIP-8360 (TCREATE opcode) to the list of Helcamine's proposals without a champion.

eips.title: Linear, Page-Based Memory Costing
eips.summary: Jochem presented linear page-based memory costing; plans to update the spec by removing memory cap and writing a report on max allocatable EVM memory.

moments.context: Jochem presented EIP-7923, explaining it replaces quadratic memory pricing with linear pricing, justified by EIP-7825. He plans to update the spec to remove the memory cap and deliver a report on maximum allocatable EVM memory within two weeks.

eips.title: Transaction Gas Limit Cap
eips.summary: Referenced as the transaction gas limit cap shipped in Fusaka that justifies removing quadratic memory pricing.

moments.context: Jochem explained that EIP-7825's transaction execution gas limit bounds make the quadratic memory cost unnecessary, since in Frontier there was no such cap.
Jochem noted the execution gas is still limited to the EIP-7825 bound of 16.7 million even after EIP-8037 introduces state gas.

eips.title: Remove storage-clear refund and refund cap
eips.summary: Jochem proposed removing refunds; Dragan suggested keeping reset-to-original refunds but removing clear-storage refunds.

moments.context: Jochem presented EIP-3298 to remove refunds, acknowledging it is outdated but the intent remains. He described storage set refunds and EIP-7702 refunds as the remaining refund spots.
Dragan argued only the clearing storage refund (X to 0) should be removed, while the reset-to-original refund (A to B to A) should stay. Jochem agreed and proposed discussing details async.

eips.title: Set Code for EOAs
eips.summary: Referenced in the context of refund removal and deprecation discussions around account abstraction.

moments.context: Jochem noted EIP-7702 Type 4 transactions create a delegation refund of 12,500 gas when the account already exists, as one of the remaining refund spots.
Chris mentioned that EIP-8130 includes 7702 deprecation as part of its spec.

eips.title: Reduction in refunds
eips.summary: Referenced as the London fork EIP that capped refunds at 20%, reducing their effectiveness.

moments.context: Jochem cited EIP-3529 as having reduced refunds to only 20% (coefficient 5), down from 50%, making them less effective and noting the old 50% was abused by gas tokens.

eips.title: PAY opcode
eips.summary: Jochem presented PAY opcode as a logical way to send ETH without executing foreign code; volunteered to champion it.

moments.context: Jochem presented EIP-5920 PAY opcode, explaining it allows sending ETH without executing foreign code, replacing the CREATE2+SELFDESTRUCT pattern. He volunteered to champion the EIP.
Lightclient noted in chat that PAY is more acceptable now that log events exist on ETH transfers.

eips.title: Deactivate SELFDESTRUCT
eips.summary: Referenced as PFI'd for Hegota; PAY opcode aligns with deactivating SELFDESTRUCT.

moments.context: Jochem noted EIP-4758 (deactivate SELFDESTRUCT) is PFI'd for Hegota and that EIP-5920 PAY creates the logical alternative for the self-destruct pattern.

eips.title: P256 algorithm support
eips.summary: Bare number appeared in nixo's reading of proposed EIP numbers but was not discussed.

moments.context: Nixo started reading out the next set of proposed EIPs, briefly mentioning 8030 as part of Dragan's PFIs before correcting to 8358.

eips.title: Net Gas Metering for Account Changes
eips.summary: Dragan presented net gas metering for account changes, discounting gas when call targets were already modified.

moments.context: Dragan presented EIP-8358, explaining it tracks whether a call target or callee was changed before and discounts roughly 4K gas when both are already changed. No questions were raised.

eips.title: Persist Warm Access Sets Across Reverts
eips.summary: Dragan presented persisting warm access sets across reverts; Danno raised concern that implementation may be harder than it looks.

moments.context: Dragan presented EIP-8374, explaining that loaded accounts and storage should remain in the access list even after reverts, as a first step toward block-wide access persistence.

Danno asked about implementation scoping, warning that cross-fork support for both modes has historically been finicky and fragile. Dragan responded it should be a small change of skipping journal entries.

eips.title: CPSB Recalibration for New Gas Limit
eips.summary: Toni presented CPSB recalibration needed for gas limit increases; described as a simple constant adjustment from EIP-8037.

moments.context: Toni explained EIP-8368 recalibrates the CPSB constant from EIP-8037, needed because the dynamic recalibration was removed. He suggested CFI'ing it depending on gas limit plans for Hegota, saying it could help push toward 600 million gas.

eips.title: eth/vhash - Blob-Aware Mempool
eips.summary: Csaba presented blob-aware mempool EIP but noted significant overlap with sparse blob pool; may fold into that work.

moments.context: Csaba presented EIP-8094, noting its goal is to avoid nasty traffic redistribution for blob fee spikes, but acknowledged roughly 90% overlap with sparse blob pool work and is considering whether to remove the EIP or focus on differences.

eips.title: eth/XX - announce transactions with nonce
eips.summary: Csaba presented announcing transactions with nonce and sender metadata to enable smarter mempool logic for scaling.

moments.context: Csaba presented EIP-8077, proposing to add metadata (nonce, sender, possibly fees) to transaction hash announcements so nodes can make more intelligent mempool decisions instead of randomly pulling hashes. Toni endorsed it in chat as helpful for frame transaction mempools.

eips.title: Precompiles for ML-DSA Verification
eips.summary: Danno presented ML-DSA precompiles using FIPS 204, arguing for all three security levels and leveraging existing library implementations.

moments.context: Danno presented EIP-8355, arguing ML-DSA is the most widely used PQ algorithm with broad language and HSM support. He diverged from prior proposals by using FIPS 204 compressed keys, providing all three security levels, and using full-width messages.
Danno addressed questions about why three precompiles are needed, explaining crypto agility if lower security levels weaken, and noting Google initially didn't even ship MLDSA44.

eips.title: Precompile for ML-DSA signature verification
eips.summary: Referenced as the prior ML-DSA precompile proposal that EIP-8355 diverges from.

moments.context: Danno noted the prior EIP-8051 used expanded 20K keys to remove bit twiddling, whereas EIP-8355 uses FIPS 204 compressed encoding of 2-4 kilobytes.

eips.title: Normalized state gas limit
eips.summary: Anders presented normalized state gas limit as a one-time calibration to adjust cost-per-state-byte and state gas limit based on observed demand.

moments.context: Anders presented EIP-8372, explaining that if demand for state creation is unexpectedly low or high after Glamsterdam, this EIP allows a one-time fork-boundary calibration of cost-per-state-byte and state gas limit by measuring state gas in normalized units.
Jochem asked whether EIP-8372 implies a state creation target. Anders confirmed it does, similar to EIP-8368, but with normalization for faster targeting based on observed demand.

eips.title: In-mempool signature and proof aggregation
eips.summary: Referenced in chat as in-mempool signature aggregation using leanSig, related to PQ signature aggregation for frames.

moments.context: Danno linked EIP-8288 in chat as relevant to aggregated PQ signature verification, noting it currently uses leanSig only.
Donnoh mentioned EIP-8288 (zkzkframes) in chat as a related add-on when discussing how 8130 composes with 8141.

eips.title: Adaptive state cost to cap growth & scale L1
eips.summary: Referenced by Anders as a prior floating-price alternative to EIP-8372's fixed calibration approach.

moments.context: Anders noted EIP-8075 does automatic adjustment with a floating price, whereas EIP-8372 provides a simpler fixed one-time solution.

eips.title: ePBS Mandatory Burn of Execution Rewards
eips.summary: Ben Adams presented ePBS mandatory burn of execution rewards using priority fee burn, builder burn target, and PTC observed floor.

moments.context: Ben Adams presented EIP-8375 (Ember), proposing burning roughly 30% of protocol-visible execution value to reduce security impact of large execution rewards, using three mechanisms: priority fee burn, external builder burn target, and PTC-observed floor.
Lightclient commented that we should see how ePBS is used in practice before building on top of it, worried builders may circumvent ePBS even with Glamsterdam.

eips.title: Checked Arithmetic Opcodes
eips.summary: Hubert Ritzdorf presented checked arithmetic opcodes for safe add/sub/mul/div; Danno questioned necessity given gas limit increases and RISC-V/WASM lacking equivalents.

moments.context: Hubert presented EIP-8219, proposing safe arithmetic opcodes that revert on overflow, reducing Solidity's 79-gas addition to a single opcode plus reducing bytecode size and deployment costs.

Danno questioned whether checked arithmetic is wise given RISC-V and WASM lack equivalents, and whether shaving gas matters as much with higher gas limits. Hubert argued going from 80 to 5 bytes for the most common DeFi operation is worthwhile.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Frame transactions debated extensively; most EL clients support it but L2s raised throughput and DoS concerns, deferring final decision to AA breakout on August 25th.

moments.context: Nixo restarted the frames discussion. Nethermind and Geth confirmed support. Ben Adams (Nethermind) said they support it as headliner. Besu said they are not in opposition. Ethrex confirmed support.
Nixo raised a comment flagging 8141 as a breaking protocol change for EVM chains that don't hard fork it, risking incompatible account standards and wallet fragmentation.
Tsahi from Offchain Labs said he supports 8141 in principle but has big problems with it as currently written, particularly around L2 sequencer economics and validation.

Felix explained that frames allow block builders to impose arbitrary limits on includeable transactions, addressing DoS concerns. Chris from Base argued 8130 provides more structural validation benefits.

Nixo deferred the decision to the AA breakout call on August 25th, asking it to produce a conclusion for the August 27th ACDE. Lightclient cautioned against losing progress made with client teams on frames.

eips.title: Keystore Accounts
eips.summary: Raised by Chris from Base as an alternative to 8141 for native AA; already shipped on Base; debate deferred to AA breakout.

moments.context: Nixo noted EIP-8130 was proposed as an alternative to 8141 but is too late to propose as a standalone EIP for Hegota.

Chris from Base argued 8130 can satisfy the same long-term Ethereum goals as frames, with structural validation in the transaction type, full key rotation, and no new opcodes. He said Base and OP are launching it.

Chris explained 8130 accounts would work on 8141 with their key info in the key store, but going the other way breaks since 8130 lacks the opcode. Felix countered that 8141's transaction assertions and post-conditions are important goals not addressed by 8130.

eips.title: Unified Transaction Content Floor
eips.summary: Referenced by Lumi as something Base can speak for themselves about, and by Daniil as buildable on top of 8141.

moments.context: Lumi mentioned 8131 in the context of letting Base speak for themselves about their proposal.
Daniil from Nethermind said in chat that 8131 can be built on top of or in parallel with 8141.
